newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed sharply lower on profit-taking after a week-long rally, but no clear trend is seen at the opening, said dealers.
"Tomorrow will be key. If the market starts rising, then the fall was just a price adjustment," said one trader.
"But if it drops steeply, this could point to a change in trend with the bolsa likely to keep on falling."
The 40-share IPSA index closed down 0.82 percent at 102.05 points. The general IGPA index shed 0.71 percent to 5,561.16 points.
Turnover remained steady at 12 billion pesos.
Most sales were by brokers trading their own accounts, said dealers.
Buying from institutional investors was light with fund managers waiting to see if the rally resumes or whether it continues to peter out, they said.

Despite the weakness, the underlying mood is positive with investors optmistic that the Central Bank will cut interest rates by the year-end as signs mount that its tight credit policy is succeeding in cooling the economy, said dealers.

This hope was reinforced by media reports that government figures to be published later this month will show economic activity slowing in August to between 4-5 percent -- its lowest level since December 1994, they said.
Losers included drug-maker LabChile, down 2.68 percent at 327 pesos, forestry firm Masisa and steel producer Cap which shed 1.49 percent at 1,325 pesos.
Winners included telecom Telex, up 0.79 percent at 1,270 pesos and winery Concha y Toro which firmed 0.63 percent to 161 pesos.
